name: Email Orders Digest
author: nwells

sections.description: Sends out a daily email digest of all orders made the previous day in WooCommerce. This provides a great summary of yesterday’s activities as well as helping with quickly checking orders against any payments received overnight without needing to log in. It can also be useful as a packing slip for a warehouse and what stock goes with which order.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/woo-email-orders directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Emails and click Manage on Daily order digest to set the recipient(s), subject, heading and introduction text, or to send a test for a chosen date
sections.faq:
What time does the email go out

By default, the emails are set in the WordPress cron scheduler at 1am. This can be adjusted using a cron interface plugin like WP Control

I didn’t receive any email overnight

The email digest currently only gets sent if an order has been made the previous day. Also check the Daily order digest email is enabled under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails.

Can I change the email layout?

Yes. The digest uses your WooCommerce email styles, header and footer. To change its body, copy templates/emails/email-orders-digest.php from the plugin to yourtheme/woocommerce/emails/email-orders-digest.php and edit it there.

I didn’t receive any email at the scheduled time

If you are relying on the built-in WordPress scheduler, then this only gets triggered by site visitors. Therefore, if no one visits your site at the exact time of your intended schedule then the email won’t trigger exactly when you want it. A preferred option, if your hosting supports, is to set up a cron task at server level to trigger the /wp-cron.php URL.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • The digest is now its own WooCommerce email: find it under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails as Daily order digest, with the usual enable/disable toggle, recipients, subject, heading and CC/BCC options. Its settings no longer appear on every email’s settings screen. Existing recipient and introduction text settings are carried over automatically
  • Multiple recipients now receive a single email addressed to all of them, as with WooCommerce’s own admin emails
  • The email body is a template that themes can override, and it can be viewed in WooCommerce’s email preview
  • Customer details in the digest are now escaped
  • Fixed a fatal error when a refund was made on the day being summarised

1.3.2

  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.1
  • Declared compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS)
  • Fixed the “View” link on each order, which was blank in the scheduled email and did not open the order when HPOS is enabled
  • Fixed the daily digest being scheduled for 1am UTC instead of 1am in the site’s timezone. Existing sites keep their current schedule; deactivate and reactivate the plugin to move it to 1am site time
  • Raised the minimum WordPress version to 6.5

1.3.1

  • Added the license to the plugin header
  • Security hardening: nonce checks and improved escaping and sanitizing

1.3.0

  • Renamed plugin to Email Order Digest
  • Tested up to WooCommerce 10.3.3
  • Update email template to use WooCommerce email styles

1.2.2

  • Allow all orders for a day to be sent rather than the default 10

1.2

  • Added a date selector to test the email digest out for a specific date

1.1

  • Added support for internationalization
  • Added support for multiple recipients – comma separated

1.0.3

  • Added sub-total, freight, discounts, and total to each order
  • Added grand total for all orders for the day

1.0.2

  • Bug fixes

1.0.1

  • Added new introduction text as an option
  • Removed cancelled orders from the email
  • Adjusted timestamp to use the correct timezone set in WP

1.0.0

  • Initial release
